thread:
Alex Chen: noticed a customer ticket — p99 latency spikes for API requests routed EU->APAC. They see TLS handshakes taking ~4-6s intermittently, causing client timeouts. raising to SRE.
Priya Rao: thanks — which customer/region and timestamps?
Alex Chen: customer id 8342, spikes around 12:10-12:35 UTC. Mostly from eu-west1 users talking to models hosted in apac-south1. p95 ok, p99 jumps.
Matt Gomez: seen similar in synthetic checks earlier this week but dismissed as noise. can you paste the apm trace ids?
Alex Chen: trace ids: trace-0a1b2c, trace-0d3e4f. here's the short stack from the app: TLS handshake -> TCP retransmit -> TLS renegotiate -> app timeout.
Ingrid Müller: can we get a traceroute/mtr from an affected client IP? also want server-side accept logs.
Rachel Li: I pulled edge logs. lots of 522/524-like timeouts at our ingress LB during those windows. SNI looks correct. no certificate errors.
sre-bot: alert: route-affinity-deviation detected on eu-pop-3 -> apac-hop-2; increased median path length by 2 AS hops.
Priya Rao: sounds like a routing/anycast shift. DNS TTLs for that customer are 60s. maybe a recursive resolver switched to a different POP and now hairpinned to apac via additional AS hop.
Matt Gomez: running quick dig+trace: 
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
34.120.45.12
$ dig +trace api.redwood.example.com
...shows eu-pop-3 -> ngix-proxy-anycast -> apac-edge-12
```
Ingrid Müller: did BGP withdraws happen around the window? ops-oncall, any bgp churn?
ops-oncall: noticed a short maintenance flap on transit provider B at 12:08 UTC, then some route updates. posting BGP dumps now.
Rachel Li: adding observability: per-token latency histograms show a long-tail correlated with increased TCP RTT and a small spike in TLS handshake retransmits.
Alex Chen: customer reported increased retries and saw 504s in their client. they attempted to retry, which amplified load.
Priya Rao: mitigation idea 1: shift DNS geo-weighting away from the affected eu POP for customers with apac backends (canary). mitigation idea 2: reduce DNS TTLs and force resolver recalc.
Matt Gomez: also can quiesce keepalives on the hairpin path and force direct egress from eu via our secondary transit (lower-cost but lower-latency for this case).
Ingrid Müller: steps to repro from eu-west: 
```
# reproduce p99: run 50 concurrent TLS handshakes to api endpoint
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -w "%{time_connect} %{time_appconnect} %{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health" & done
```
You should see some appconnect > 3s when route is hairpinned.

Priya Rao: quick checks executed:
- ran mtr from eu-pop-3 -> apac-edge-12: intermittent 200-400ms hops at asn-xyz
- packet capture shows TLS ClientHello retransmit before server ServerHello

ops-oncall: temporary mitigation applied: adjusted DNS weight for eu-west to favor eu-pop-1 and eu-pop-2; lowered TTL to 30s. rolling now (canary 5% -> 25%).
Alex Chen: customer notified of mitigation and asked for eta.
Rachel Li: also enabling automatic fallback in routing policy: when median handshake > 1s for 2m, route to backup region (config name: route_policy/fallback-handshake-v1). staging push ready.
Matt Gomez: please be careful — fallback risks cross-region cost and may increase token egress. add to incident notes for billing ops.
Ingrid Müller: permanent fix candidates: talk to transit provider to see if we can prevent the specific AS path change, or add more POPs in APAC to reduce hairpin. also consider adjusting our anycast origin weights.
Priya Rao: action items: 
- @ops-oncall: keep DNS weight adjustment for 20 minutes and monitor p99 (owner: ops-oncall).
- @Matt Gomez: prepare a rollback in case new route causes regressions (owner: Matt).
- @Rachel Li: add synthetic canary to hit eu->apac model path every 30s and alert on handshake >1s (owner: Rachel).
- @Ingrid Müller: collect PCAP and BGP dump and open ticket with transit provider (owner: Ingrid).

ops-oncall: DNS canary is at 20% now — p99 dropped from ~5.8s to ~1.2s for affected customers. still monitoring.
Alex Chen: thanks team. I've asked the customer to hold off retries and to increase client timeout to 10s as temporary client-side mitigation.
Priya Rao: note for postmortem: document how geo-DNS weights and BGP churn interact to create hairpinning and TLS handshake inflation. recommend automated detection (we have heuristics but need a tuned rule).
Matt Gomez: can we add a small jitter to DNS TTL reductions to avoid synchronized resolver thrash?
Ingrid Müller: good call. also add a runbook entry under eng-sre/route-affinity for step-by-step. I'll draft.
Rachel Li: will follow up with dashboards updated and synthetic alerts within 2 hours.
Alex Chen: closing the customer escalation once p99 stable for 30m. will update thread. :thumbsup: 
ops-oncall: 1998765700 — p99 stable at ~900ms for 35m. leaving DNS weights back to normal gradually.
Alex Chen: thread resolution: keep postmortem and runbook, ops ticket opened with transit provider (TP-4579).
